evals.name: production-rules-while-writing
evals.setup: An agent has read the skill as context and is about to edit `service.go` — production code, not a test file.
evals.query: Add a Close method to the Service type in service.go

evals.name: test-rules-inherit-production
evals.setup: The same agent then writes `service_test.go`, including a table test and a helper.
evals.query: Write tests for Service.Close in service_test.go

evals.name: pass-lists-offenses-then-asks
evals.setup: `./pkg/foo` has a single-letter receiver and a godoc on an interface-implementing method. It also has an off-by-one in a loop bound — a correctness bug, not a style offense.

evals.name: fix-applies-everything-behind-a-green-gate
evals.setup: `./pkg/foo` has six offenses. The module test suite is green before the run.

evals.name: delegated-by-review
evals.setup: `go:review` is running a check on the current diff and invokes `style` for the style dimension.

evals.name: rules-change-only-through-review
evals.setup: The user asks `style` directly to add a new rule.
evals.query: /style add a rule that test helpers never return errors

evals.name: broad-target-auto-plan-first
evals.setup: A 12-package module. Every package holds the same four offenses — a `%v` error wrap, a single-letter receiver, missing godoc on an exported symbol, and a missing blank line between test topic groups — so 48 offenses fold to 4 findings. Two packages hold three further offenses each that no other package has, giving 54 in all and 10 findings after folding. Invoked with no budget controls, so the proposed default cap is 25: the cap binds on the unfolded list and does not bind on the folded one, which is the difference the run has to get right.

evals.name: incidental-interface-satisfaction
evals.setup: A package where `(*Conn).Close` is pinned by `var _ io.Closer = (*Conn)(nil)` and carries a full godoc restating the contract, and `(*Buffer).Close` is simply this type's own cleanup — no assertion, no interface named in its docs — but `goToImplementation` reports it as satisfying `io.Closer` all the same. Both have godoc.

evals.name: severity-and-ids-are-stable
evals.setup: Three packages carrying the same two offenses each: a single-letter receiver and an exported symbol with no godoc. Small enough to check in one context, so nothing merges — the point is whether one run is self-consistent across packages.
